MIND. [1] [Am. c.]
Listlessness and lethargy. θ Hysteria.
Utter dejection of mind. θ Chlorosis.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Am. c.]
Feeling of lightness in head.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Am. c.]
Heaviness and beating in forehead after dinner.
Sense of oppressive fulness, pushing as if forehead would burst.
Severe pain in forehead. θ Undeveloped measles.
Pulsating, beating and pressing in forehead, as if it would burst ; worse after eating ; while walking in open air ; better from pressure ; in warm room.
Headache, thrusts in forehead, as if it would burst.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Am. c.]
Sparks before eyes at night. θ Headache.
Large black spot floats before eyes after sewing.
Eyes weak and watery, especially after reading ; muscular asthenopia ; affections from overstraining eyes.
Yellow spots on looking at white objects.
Cataract of right eye.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Am. c.]
Hard hearing ; ear itches and discharges pus.
Hard swelling of right parotid gland. θ Scarlatina.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Am. c.]
Nosebleed ; severe pain as if brain was forcing itself out just above nose.
Nosebleed : when washing face or hands in morning nose bleeds from left nostril ; from right several days in succession, weakening boy. θ Undeveloped measles.
When stooping, blood rushes to tip of nose.
Bloody mucus blown from nose frequently. θ Ozæna.
Burning water runs from nose ; < when stooping.
Stoppage, mostly at night ; must breathe through mouth, with long-lasting coryza. θ Scarlatina.
Child's nose stopped up, starts from sleep ; rattling of phlegm in trachea.
Coryza in hysterical females, in feeble or aged people.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Am. c.]
Swelling of internal mouth, especially inside of cheeks.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Am. c.]
Enlarged tonsils, bluish, much offensive mucus there. θ Scarlatina.
Putrid sore throat ; glands engorged. θ Scarlatina.
Tendency to gangrenous ulceration of tonsils. θ Scarlatina.
Angina after checking an old ulcer on leg ; ceased when ulcer returned.
Burning pain in throat and down œsophagus as from alcohol.
Roughness and scraping in throat.
Diphtheria, when nose is stopped up ; child starts from sleep, cannot get its breath.
Diphtheria ; nose stopped both sides, membrane extends to upper lip, which is excoriated from watery discharge.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Am. c.]
Pressure in stomach after eating or at night ; clothes feel oppressive.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Am. c.]
Splenic affections.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Am. c.]
Colic with pain between scapulæ. θ Amenorrhœa.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Am. c.]
Costiveness on account of hardness of feces.
Constipation ; stool hard and dry, difficult to expel, with headache.
Constipation with hemorrhoids.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Am. c.]
Frequent urination at night.
Involuntary urination during sleep ; urine pale with red sediment.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Am. c.]
Great excitement of female sexual organs. θ Hysteria.
Cholera-like symptoms at commencement of catamenia.
During catamenia : toothache ; colic ; face pale ; very sad ; great fatigue, especially of thighs, with yawning, toothache, pain in small of back and chilliness.
The courses come on six days too soon.
The menstrual blood is blackish, often in clots, passing off with spasmodic pain in belly and hard stools, with tenesmus ; flow abundant.
Menstrual blood acrid, makes thighs sore ; soreness causes a burning pain.
Acrid leucorrhœa, with sensation of excoriation or ulceration in vulva. θ Hysteria.
Leucorrhœa : watery, burning, from uterus ; acrid, profuse, from vagina.
Violent tearing in abdomen and vagina.
Irritation of clitoris. θ Hysteria.
Swelling, itching and burning of pudenda.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Am. c.]
Accumulation of mucus in trachea. θ Softening of brain.
Catarrh.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Am. c.]
Great difficulty of breathing in going up even a few steps ; less in open air.
Dares not come into a warm room, in which he becomes deathly pale and can do nothing but sit quiet. θ Asthma.
Difficult breathing ; causing short cough.
Oppression of breathing.
Catarrh, dyspnœa, asthma.
One of the best remedies in emphysema.
Œdema pulmonum with somnolence from poisoning of blood with carbonic acid.
   

COUGH. [27] [Am. c.]
Cough at night ; every morning, at 3 o'clock, dry cough from tickling in throat, as of dust.
Cough : with spitting of blood, previous sweet taste and great dyspnœa, with stitches in small of back and pit of stomach ; short, asthmatic, from irritation in larynx, with painful sensation of spasmodic contraction of chest ; with asthma, evening in bed ; with hoarseness, body being warm ; with spitting of bloody phlegm, Sputa thin, foamy ; adynamic state, with rattling of large bubbles in chest. θ Bronchitis in the aged.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Am. c.]
Burning in chest ; also with hydrothorax.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Am. c.]
Vehement palpitation of heart and great precordial distress, followed by syncope. θ Hysteria.
Palpitation of heart. θ Headache.
Palpitation and asthma after every exertion.
Pulse hard, tense, frequent.
Angina pectoris.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Am. c.]
Pain between scapulæ.
Violent pain in small of back, with great coldness. θ Amenorrhœa.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Am. c.]
Panaritium ; finger inflamed ; deep-seated periosteal pain.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Am. c.]
Heel hurts when standing or walking much ; sometimes suppuration.
Ball of great toe painful and hot.
Feet and toes swollen.
Crawling in toes.
   

NERVES. [36] [Am. c.]
Exhaustion with defective reaction.
Hysteria with symptoms simulating organic affections.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Am. c.]
Frequent violent starting out of sleep, with great fear afterwards.
Nightmare every night, sometimes in a sweat when awaking. θ Heart disease.
Somnolence, with blood overcarbonized. θ Œdema pulmonum.
Heart-beats disturb sleep ; stupor. θ Scarlatina.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Am. c.]
In wet, stormy weather : ill humor ; < headache.
Very sensitive to cold air out-doors.
Children dislike washing.
In a warm room : headache > ; get deathly pale. θ Asthma.
Averse to walking in open air.
Aversion to walking in open air.
   

FEVER. [40] [Am. c.]
Hectic fever. θ Scurvy.
Cold, cyanotic, semiconscious, pulseless. θ Beginning of spotted fever.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Am. c.]
Outer pressure : headache > ; constrictive pain in stomach > ; pain in bowels >.
After a fall from a horse and sprain of left great toe, frequent inflammation, joint red, hot and painful, and so sensitive to touch that he could not bear the bedcovers ; continual sensation as if joint was dislocated.
   

SKIN. [46] [Am. c.]
Violent itching ; after scratching, burning blisters appear.
Desquamation.
Putrid flat ulcers with a pungent sensation, pain > by keeping limb elevated and from outward pressure ; pus white and putrid.
Brought out measles after three months' delay.
Body red as if covered with scarlatina.
Malignant scarlatina with somnolence, starting from sleep ; dark red or putrid sore throat ; sticky salivation ; parotitis ; external throat swollen ; stertorous breathing ; involuntary stools with excessive vomiting ; body red, with miliary rash, or faintly developed eruption ; threatened paralysis of brain.
Scarlatina receding.
Erysipelas of old people when cerebral symptoms are developed ; while eruption is still out, debility and soreness of whole body ; tendency to gangrenous destruction.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Am. c.]
Scrofulous children.
Stout women, who lead a sedentary life, have various troubles in consequence, and readily catch cold in winter.
